chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mubarik, from Abi Maryam al-Asbahani, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about drinking the milk of donkeys, and he said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is drinking donkey milk permissible in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith highlights the distinct juristic treatment of donkey milk compared to donkey meat, which is subject to greater debate among schools of thought. The Imam’s concise ruling of 'no harm' (la ba's biha) establishes its permissibility (jawaaz), reflecting the principle that the prohibition of meat does not automatically extend to its byproducts unless specified. This distinction underscores the nuanced approach of Shia fiqh in differentiating between various animal derivatives based on specific textual evidence.
